items.Sentence: Headworks consists of an influent flow meter, a submersible pump station (including backup), and two ¼” step screens, in a two-channel system to allow for redundancy.
After the screens, wastewater flows into a vortex aerated grit chamber with a bypass channel and primary clarifier splitter box.
Headworks consists of an influent flow meter, a submersible pump station (including backup), and two ¼” step screens... the four influent pumps are sized for 2,100 gallons per minute (gpm) each.
Wastewater flows into the primary clarifier splitter box after degritting.

The primary clarifier splitter box splits high salt flow and low salt flow. High salts flow goes to the high TDS pond, while low salts flow normally goes to the aeration basin/mixed liquor splitter box.

Secondary treatment systems for low salts wastewater consists of an aeration basin/mixed liquor splitter box, three aeration basins, two secondary clarifiers, a return activated sludge (RAS) and wasted activated sludge (WAS) pump station, and two equalization ponds.

The aeration basins are sized for 3.2 mgd and a solids retention time (SRT) of 12 days. Each aeration basin has six zones and bypassing capabilities with various settings for anaerobic, anoxic, or oxic functions.
Secondary treatment systems for low salts wastewater consists of ... two secondary clarifiers...
Secondary treatment systems for low salts wastewater consists of ... a return activated sludge (RAS) and wasted activated sludge (WAS) pump station...
Biological and filtered treatment for high salt concentration wastewater is performed by a membrane bioreactor (MBR).

When high salt concentrations are detected by an electroconductivity meter in the primary clarifier splitter box, wastewater is redirected as high salt flow to 1 mm rotary drum screens with flows directed to a shotcrete-lined high TDS pond.
Filtration of the low salt concentration wastewater stream is performed by the UF membrane facility.
The high salts treatment train flows from the MBR to a reverse osmosis (RO) system for advanced treatment.
Each of the three units houses a cartridge filter assembly and 40 spiral wound medium pressure membranes contained in 8 pressure vessels in a 4:2:1:1 four stage array.
The UV disinfection system disinfects the comingled flows from the background UF permeate (low TDS treatment train) and the RO permeate (high TDS treatment train).
Solids from the two secondary clarifiers are sent to concrete lined beds for drying and hauled off annually to the Engel & Gray composting facility.
Disinfected tertiary recycled water is held in short term storage (currently two one-million-gallon (mg) aboveground steel welded tanks) at the plant and distributed to offsite users.

Chemical additives are used to maintain the functions of filters, to adjust pH, and to ensure clean tanks and piping. Laguna County Sanitation District reported the following chemical additives to the treatment system and the reason for their use. • Sodium Hypochlorite 12.5% - 3,200 gallons per month. Required for UF and MBR membrane cleaning. • Sodium Hypochlorite 12.5% – 930 gallons per month. Applied to keep recycled water piping and tanks clean. • Citric Acid 50% - 1,000 gallons per month. Required for UF and MBR membrane cleaning. • Sulfuric Acid 93% - 600 gallons per month. Required for pH control of RO feed water. • Aqua Ammonia 29.4% - 150 gallons per month. Required to convert free chlorine to chloramines in RO feed water. • Antiscalant – 300 gallons per month. Required to maintain RO elements.
